summary: Accepted ADR establishing Hoplight's canonical superset and escrow model. Its schema-authority note records that ADR-011 supersedes the original Zod-under-packages/core wording: current domain contracts are handwritten interfaces in src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts paired with exhaustive adjacent runtime decoders. The Decision retains one canonical model per content type, carries fields without a canonical home in origin-keyed escrow, merges escrow for semantically identical same-format round trips, and requires honest reports for cross-format loss or recovery through tolerated extension fields. Why not "just use chara_card_v3 internally" explains that V3 covers cards only and cannot represent all RoleCall, Risu, Backyard, lorebook, preset, or persona meaning. Precedents in the author's own earlier code identifies RoleCall unsupportedFields and origin plus VAUDEVILLE normalizers as earlier forms of the pattern. Consequences requires codec capability tables to drive conversion reporting and the generated support matrix, while changes to canonical domain contracts demand a migration note, fixture sweep, and explicit design review. ADR-005's superset, escrow envelope, and Round-Trip Law remain accepted even though ADR-011 now owns runtime schema authority.

sections.title: Decision
sections.summary: The decision text defines one canonical superset per content type and an origin-keyed escrow envelope for fields without a canonical home. Its parse and serialize equations require reports at both boundaries. Same-format serialization merges escrow so the result remains semantically identical under the Round-Trip Law. Cross-format serialization expresses supported meaning, reports escrowed or dropped fields, and preserves escrow where the target permits extension fields, allowing later recovery. The section's historical statement places Zod schemas in packages/core, but the document's schema-authority note explicitly supersedes that detail through ADR-011. Current authority is handwritten domain interfaces under src/entities/<kind>/schema.ts paired with exhaustive runtime decoders; the superset and escrow behavior itself is unchanged.

sections.title: Why not "just use chara_card_v3 internally"
sections.summary: V3 is card-only and still lossy against RoleCall details palette sprites and depth-injections, Risu extensions, and Backyard fields. Lorebooks, presets, and personas need models V3 does not define. A superset with escrow means the project never argues with a format author about whose fields matter.

sections.title: Precedents in the author's own earlier code
sections.summary: RoleCall LorebookEntry unsupportedFields and origin fields are this escrow pattern in miniature. VAUDEVILLE normalizers already unify V1 V2 V3 rcpersona and RoleOut into a common shape. This ADR promotes that established habit into a system-wide law rather than inventing a new approach.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.summary: Every codec ships a capabilities table mapping canonical field to native, escrow, or dropped that powers honest conversion reports and the docs format-support matrix which is auto-generated and never hand-maintained. core schema changes are the most expensive changes in the repo: they require a migration note, a fixture sweep, and explicit design review.
